units.translation: O most unhappy of all maidens, who loosen their girdles at their ruin. But instead of the girdle and belt he now said στρόφον [twisted band].
the whole land through which holy Strymon flows
bedding and the presence of just eyes
where Elmsley reads στορνύναι [to spread] at Eur. Med. 1209.
to whom the task has been assigned to strew the floor of the path with tapestries
nor, having strewn the way with garments, make it a path that invites envy
a cowardly lion turning about in its lair
It is almost the same as ἀστεργάνωρ [man-hating], which itself is also found only in Aeschylus.
you will come against the army of the Amazons, man-hating
Thus Hermann for στύγειον [hateful], which Turnebus had changed to στυγερὸν [hateful].
to traverse the hateful road of the house
having met with this hateful fate
hands not holy, hateful because of these things
you were destroyed by a hateful death
it has been decided to display a hateful Muse
where in M is written εἴργων [shutting in], from which Wakefield restored στέγων [covering].
Why do you not hate the god most hateful to the gods?
if it is a disease to hate one's enemies
he hates the feast of the eagles
but the one you should love, you hate
having well hated the insolence of men, may you escape
I will entreat the greatly hated one
the whole race of Laius was hated by Phoebus
for some Stygian mist hovers over
of hateful ruin upon the waves
hateful indeed are Athens to enemies
speaking hateful words of ill omen
of a detestable thing or crime
where Enger restored στύγος φρενῶν [hatred of the mind], as at 1308 εἴ τι μὴ φρενῶν στύγος [unless there is some hatred of the mind].
Of the dragon. Which the scholiast explains by τοῦ μισητοῦ θηρίου [the hateful beast]. In M ὑποστύγος, which Schuetz corrected.
From where did this hostile hatred come upon the army?
Do not report these things to the master's hatred
and she who devised this hatred against her husband
and on land there was even more hatred
I say that I will kill my mother not without justice, a father-murdering pollution and hatred of the gods
O all-hated beasts, hatreds of the gods
O god-mad and great hatred of the gods
And how was the udder unwounded by the hatred?
unless there is some hatred of the mind
